response.title: Hippowdon
paragraphs: Hippowdon is a slow support setter with Yawn, Stealth Rock, and Whirlwind to pressure switches and shape the pace of a battle; Earthquake is its sole attack. Its final stats are 215 HP, 154 Defense, and 124 Special Defense, with the 32 Stat Points in HP and Special Defense and only 2 in Defense. Impish is its nature, but the displayed allocation—not the nature label—shows where most of its investment lies.

Sand Stream gives the team weather pressure, but sand damage can chip Meowscarada and break the full-HP condition for Focus Sash if Meowscarada remains active through an affected end-of-turn tick. This is a timing and positioning concern, not a battle-start loss of the item: use Meowscarada before sand damage accumulates or keep it off the field during those ticks. Hippowdon is weak to Water, Grass, and Ice; the supplied profiles show Salamence Mega and Archaludon resist Water, Salamence Mega resists Grass, and Lucario Mega Z resists Ice, though resistance alone does not establish a safe switch-in.

recommendations.title: Plan Meowscarada’s Focus Sash around Hippowdon’s sand turns.
recommendations.reason: Sand Stream’s residual damage can remove Meowscarada’s full-HP condition if it is active at an affected end-of-turn tick. Lead or deploy it before that chip, or preserve it off the field while sand is active; the item is not automatically broken when battle begins.

recommendations.title: Use Hippowdon to establish hazards and force choices before committing an attacker.
recommendations.reason: Stealth Rock creates switch-in pressure, while Yawn can threaten sleep after a turn and Whirlwind can force a switch. Earthquake is its only selected attack, so use the faster teammates to capitalize on the openings rather than expecting Hippowdon to supply broad attacking coverage.
